verses.text: The prophet Elisha called a man from the group of prophets and said to him, "Tuck your cloak into your belt, take this small jar of olive oil, and go to Ramoth Gilead.
When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi. Go to him, get him away from his companions, and take him into an inner room.
Then take the jar of oil, pour it on his head, and say, 'This is what the LORD says: I have anointed you king over Israel.' Then open the door and run. Do not wait."
So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth Gilead.
When he arrived, he found the army commanders sitting together. He said, "I have a message for you, commander." Jehu asked, "For which of us?" He answered, "For you, commander."

So Jehu got up and went into the house. The young prophet poured the oil on his head and said, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I have anointed you king over the LORD's people Israel.
You must destroy the family of your master Ahab. In this way I will punish Jezebel for the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the LORD's servants she killed.
Ahab's whole family will die. I will cut off every male in Ahab's family in Israel, slave or free.
I will make Ahab's family like the family of Jeroboam son of Nebat and the family of Baasha son of Ahijah.
Dogs will eat Jezebel on the land at Jezreel, and no one will bury her.'" Then he opened the door and ran away.

When Jehu went back out to his master's officers, one of them asked him, "Is everything all right? Why did this crazy man come to you?" Jehu answered, "You know the man and the kind of things he says."
They said, "That's not true! Tell us." So Jehu said, "He told me, 'This is what the LORD says: I have anointed you king over Israel.'"
At once each of them took off his cloak and spread it under Jehu on the bare steps. Then they blew the trumpet and shouted, "Jehu is king!"
So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi, made a plot against Joram. At that time Joram and all Israel had been guarding Ramoth Gilead against Hazael king of Syria.

But King Joram had gone back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Syrians had given him in the battle with Hazael king of Syria. Jehu said, "If you are with me, do not let anyone slip out of the city to go and warn Jezreel."
Then Jehu got into his chariot and rode to Jezreel, because Joram was lying there wounded. Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to visit Joram.
The lookout standing on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's troops coming. He called out, "I see a group of soldiers." Joram said, "Send a horseman to meet them and ask, 'Do you come in peace?'"

So a horseman rode out to meet Jehu and said, "The king asks, 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu answered, "What do you care about peace? Get behind me!" The lookout reported, "The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back."
So the king sent out a second horseman. He came to them and said, "The king asks, 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu answered, "What do you care about peace? Get behind me!"
The lookout reported, "He reached them, but he is not coming back either. The driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi. He drives like a madman."

Joram ordered, "Get my chariot ready." When it was ready, Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah rode out, each in his own chariot, to meet Jehu. They met him at the field that had belonged to Naboth from Jezreel.
When Joram saw Jehu, he asked, "Do you come in peace, Jehu?" Jehu answered, "How can there be peace while your mother Jezebel's idol worship and witchcraft are everywhere?"
Joram turned his chariot around and ran away, shouting to Ahaziah, "Treason, Ahaziah!"
Jehu pulled back his bow with all his strength and shot Joram between the shoulders. The arrow went through his heart, and he fell down dead in his chariot.

Jehu said to Bidkar, his chariot officer, "Pick him up and throw him into the field that belonged to Naboth from Jezreel. Remember when you and I were riding together behind his father Ahab, and the LORD spoke this message against him:

'Yesterday I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, says the LORD, and I will surely pay you back on this very piece of land, says the LORD.' So pick him up and throw him onto that land, just as the LORD said."

When Ahaziah king of Judah saw what happened, he ran away along the road to Beth Haggan. Jehu chased him, shouting, "Kill him too!" They shot him in his chariot on the way up to Gur, near Ibleam. He escaped to Megiddo and died there.
His officials carried his body in a chariot to Jerusalem and buried him with his ancestors in his tomb in the city of David.
Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year that Joram son of Ahab was king of Israel.
Then Jehu came to Jezreel. When Jezebel heard about it, she put on eye makeup, fixed her hair, and looked out of a window.
As Jehu came through the gate, she called out, "Have you come in peace, you Zimri, you murderer of your master?"
Jehu looked up at the window and called, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three palace officials looked down at him.
Jehu said, "Throw her down!" So they threw her down. Some of her blood splashed on the wall and on the horses, and the horses trampled her.
Jehu went inside and ate and drank. Then he said, "Take care of that cursed woman and bury her, because she was a king's daughter."
But when they went to bury her, they found nothing left except her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands.
They went back and told Jehu. He said, "This is what the LORD said through his servant Elijah from Tishbe: 'On the land at Jezreel, dogs will eat Jezebel's flesh.
Jezebel's body will be like dung spread on the field in the land of Jezreel, so that no one will be able to say, "This is Jezebel."'"
